name: Kentucky Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Hot Browns, Burgoo & Bourbon
description:
Kentucky's restaurants, from a Hot Brown at the hotel that created it to mutton and burgoo in Owensboro.

Kentucky Eats is a free guide to eating in Kentucky: 9 places for a Hot Brown, 6 Kentucky classics from burgoo to beer cheese, 8 tables in Bardstown and bourbon country, 9 Covington and Newport picks and 4 historic inns and taverns we checked by hand, plus 8,659 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 377 towns, from Louisville and Lexington to Paducah and Pikeville. No account, no ads.

KENTUCKY GUIDES
• Hot Browns: from the Brown Hotel, where the dish was created in 1926, to Frankfort's Hot Brown Trail.
• Kentucky Classics: Owensboro mutton and burgoo, beer cheese, rolled oysters and spoonbread.
• Bardstown & Bourbon Country: dinner between distillery tours.
• Covington & Newport: goetta, a German beer hall and river-town dining.
• Historic Inns & Taverns: from 1779 to the Beaumont Inn.
• James Beard Honors and Oldest Places.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "hot brown", "bardstown", "moonlite".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 source or a Kentucky tourism office's own page. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested in the states that publish official restaurant lists, plus Louisville Metro's permitted restaurants. Louisville places also show Louisville Metro's official inspection score, and its own A, B or C grade where it gave one, as published and dated; every other place links its county's page on Kentucky's public inspection site. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Kentucky Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Louisville Metro Government or any health department), the Kentucky Distillers' Association, or the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others, and from Louisville Metro Open Data (public domain, PDDL); sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Kentucky Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Kentucky (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: Hot Browns, Kentucky classics (burgoo, mutton, beer cheese, rolled oysters, spoonbread), Bardstown and bourbon-country dining, Covington and Newport, and historic inns and taverns, 34 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard Foundation's honorees. It also lists 8,659 restaurants, cafés and bars in 377 towns from open map data and Louisville Metro's open records. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Hot Browns (or Kentucky Classics, Bardstown & Bourbon Country, Covington & Newport, Historic Inns & Taverns, James Beard Honors, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, Louisville places show Louisville Metro's official inspection score (and its own letter grade where it gave one) with the date, and every other place has a link that opens its county's page on Kentucky's public inspection site in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("hot brown", "bardstown", "moonlite").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Kentucky (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Kentucky, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Kentucky Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Kentucky Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Kentucky Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); Louisville Metro's food permits, inspections and alcohol licenses (Louisville Metro Open Data, public domain under the PDDL); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and official tourism pages.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/kentucky-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Kentucky; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Inspection results appear only for Louisville Metro, as it published them, with the date; the app computes no grades and ranks nothing by inspections. Alcohol licenses are shown only where Louisville Metro publishes them. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.
